timeline.title: A Short History of Graduation Day
items: A woman builds a school
Fatima al-Fihri founded al-Qarawiyyin in Fez. It is still teaching students today.
The first university
Students in Bologna came together to learn, and the idea of a university was born.
Four women graduate
The University of London awarded degrees to women for the first time. Four of them.
Hats in the air
New officers at the US Naval Academy threw their caps skyward, starting a tradition the world copied.
today: Not in the history books yet. Give it time. We already know how this story goes.

facts.title: The Science of a Brilliant Mind
items: cap
A builder's hat
The flat graduation cap is called a mortarboard, after the board builders use to hold mortar.
key
One step up
Graduation comes from the Latin word gradus, which means a step. And what a step it is.
pulse
A brand new brain
Learning really changes the brain. Every new skill builds fresh connections between nerve cells.
moon
Sleep is studying
While you sleep, your brain sorts and stores what you learned that day. Naps count.
clock
Cramming loses
Little and often beats one giant all nighter. Scientists call it the spacing effect.
star
Curiosity pays
Being curious about a subject helps the brain remember it, and other things learned at the same time.
facts.hand: Science can explain a lot. It still cannot explain how {who} did it on that much coffee.

note.title: What we believe a graduate is
paras: We make magazines for a living, but some feel different. This was one of them.
We believe graduation is not only the cap and the gown. It is every early start, every page read twice, every time you nearly quit and kept going anyway.
{who}, someone wanted you to have something special. Not a card anyone could buy, but pages full of you: your face, your words, the long road that brought you here.
That someone is {from}. And from everything they told us, they could not be prouder of you.
